title: Reinhardt's Maximum-Perimeter Polygon Problem for n=16, 32, and 64
summary: A convex polygon is called small if its diameter is at most one. Reinhardt proved the universal perimeter bound $\operatorname{perim}(P)\le U_n:=2n\sin(π/(2n))$, and the bound is attained whenever $n$ has a nontrivial odd divisor. The remaining power-of-two cases have resisted exact solution beyond $n=8$. We give computer-assisted proofs of the first three cases, $n=16,32,64$, and in each case prove uniqueness of the maximizing congruence class.
